summary: SL-101 followed up SL-056's unkept promise to record Controlled Folder Access (CFA) next to the fsutil last-access state. It built a never-throw Windows PowerShell 5.1 Defender read (tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/DefenderState.cs), a 65-test class with a 17-row placeholder corpus, one record line written by HeldOpenTreeTests.Record(), and a person-run recipe in docs/design/SL-101-controlled-folder-access.md. The question that opened it (does a CFA-protected folder block or notify on the FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES keep-open, Q-101) is not answered. Arming CFA needs an administrator, Windows Sandbox cannot run Defender, and a toast needs a person. Only the CFA-off blocks of the recipe were run.

payload.reason: Criterion 1 is built and validated (870 of 870 tests passed, the record line prints beside the fsutil line). Criteria 2 and 3 and Q-101 need an administrator and a person at the desktop. They are filed for a person and were not answered.
payload.summary: SL-101 followed up SL-056's unkept promise to record Controlled Folder Access (CFA) next to the fsutil last-access state. It built a never-throw Windows PowerShell 5.1 Defender read (tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/DefenderState.cs), a 65-test class with a 17-row placeholder corpus, one record line written by HeldOpenTreeTests.Record(), and a person-run recipe in docs/design/SL-101-controlled-folder-access.md. The question that opened it (does a CFA-protected folder block or notify on the FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES keep-open, Q-101) is not answered. Arming CFA needs an administrator, Windows Sandbox cannot run Defender, and a toast needs a person. Only the CFA-off blocks of the recipe were run.

lessons_judged.why: Every test, publish and the recipe's publish step went through eng/dotnet.ps1. The pwsh-7 parent of testhost is what made the PSModulePath case relevant.
The recipe publishes the exe and scans with eng/read-window.ps1 -Root. Code review checked the recipe's Scan helper fields against WindowReport.cs:217-225 for schema 1.
W-001's checker and its oracle corpus were not touched. This slice added no window case or rule-checker script.

The design kept LastAccessAsked/Kept internal (Q-159) and observes kept versus fell-back from outside, through 1123/1124 events and the 48 h back-dated last-access witness (review M3). It did not trust spike #109's internal counters as a public shape.

This is why no opt-in CFA=on Fact was built: it would have cost a Trait, an FsaDefaultTestFilter clause and an OptInTraitTests pin. The new class carries no Trait, Skip or Explicit, and OptInTraitTests and CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped pass.
It kept any CFA Fact out of LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests, whose Fact set is pinned. LastAccessRuleCorpusTests was untouched.
The recipe roots its fixtures under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp, never %TEMP%. The build also had to drop Path.GetTempPath() from the missing-exe Fact to satisfy the temp-route Fitness rules.

The survey marked criteria 2 and 3 checked_by person up front, so the design built nothing to judge them. The lesson does not stop a person-only slice from being sized and reviewed like a full medium slice.

payload.estimate_error: Sized by a person at medium size and medium risk, and wrong in two directions. The review effort was too big for the surface touched: only tests/, docs/ and .taad/fitness.yaml changed, and src/ was untouched. It still ran critique twice, code review twice and validate twice, drew 13 findings (8 + 5), and left 10 minors waived to SC-275..SC-284 plus 3 preconditions at SC-287..SC-289. It was too small in the one way that mattered: 2 of 3 derived criteria were person-only, known at the survey, so 'complete' meant 'record line and untested recipe', not an answer to Q-101. The review volume tracked the number of default-suite Facts added (about 65 tests in DefenderStateRecordTests), not the lines of product code.
what_went_wrong: The survey reported 'allowed-apps list has 1 entry' from an unelevated read. That was the placeholder 'N/A: Must be an administrator to view exclusions', not a count. The design copied it into the Describe contract as the expected reading ('allowed apps=1'). It was caught by the first critique (M1) and confirmed in build by a 17-row corpus (9 placeholder rows red before the fix, 8 real rows green). The cost was a major finding, a rewritten contract and a new corpus file.

The builder added two Facts the design never listed: TheLineAgreesWithAFreshReadOnThisPc and TheChildPowerShellStartsWithItsOwnModulePath. Both assert machine-dependent state, against the design's own 'nothing turns red'. They drew m1 and R2-m4. Both were waived (SC-282, SC-283), so the shipped default suite can go red on Defender in Passive, SxS Passive or EDR Block mode (the AMRunningMode=\S+ regex rejects those names) and on a PC with a foreign '...\PowerShell\Modules' entry in its machine or user PSModulePath.

Describe's 'total, never throws' contract was false when it shipped (R2-m5, SC-284). A lone surrogate throws InvalidOperationException or ArgumentException past `catch (JsonException)`. The comments at DefenderState.cs:58 and :119 still claim totality. Only ReadOnce's catch-all keeps the production line safe.

Validate halted once on O-014, O-015 and O-016, the three administrator-gated must-verify preconditions design-slice had routed to validate. Code review had already said (m3) that they belong with the person, and build documented that. The obligation rows stayed open until the loop waived them to SC-287..SC-289. That was an extra validate lap with no code change.

The headline question (Q-101) is unanswered. Only the CFA-off blocks of the recipe were run, at Medium integrity. The first real execution is a person's single administrator session, and Q-235 and lesson #340 say a never-run recipe draws findings.

Code review's first pass missed R2-m4 and R2-m5. Both surfaced only in the second round, when the reviewer explicitly tried to break the code, and R2-m4 was a sibling of the round-1 m1 defect it had just filed.

missed.what: The design imported three administrator-gated must-verify preconditions (published exe is the image CFA judges, a custom folder is judged like Documents, the person can arm CFA) as validate-slice obligations. The critique did not ask of each must-verify invariant whether any unattended stage can arm it. None can: the Sandbox has no Defender and arming needs an administrator. The rule is already recorded as lesson #398 and CC-006. Cost: validate-slice #1 halted on O-014..O-016 until they were waived to SC-287..SC-289.

The design's 'a missing property prints ?' case rested on recalled ConvertTo-Json behaviour, listed as 'recalled' in outside_claims. The real 5.1 child builds a [pscustomobject] with every key and a missing cmdlet property serialises as null, never as an absent key. A one-line powershell.exe measurement settles it. The critique measured the allowed-apps placeholder but not this.

The critique did not check the design's missing-exe Fact against the existing temp-route Fitness rules (the SL-096 SystemRootTempRoute patterns over tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests). The first build used Path.GetTempPath() for the non-existent path and broke the rule. The fix was a name under AppContext.BaseDirectory.

TheChildPowerShellStartsWithItsOwnModulePath asserts no child PSModulePath entry matches (?i)(?<![a-z])PowerShell\\(7\\)?Modules. That also matches any foreign '...\PowerShell\Modules' entry, such as SQL Server tools in the machine value, so the default suite goes red where the strip works. The first review pass had just filed the identical failure class on the sibling Fact (m1) and did not audit the other machine-state Fact.

Describe and Read claim 'Total / never throws' (DefenderState.cs:58, :119). An escaped lone surrogate ('\ud800abc') makes GetString() throw InvalidOperationException, and a raw lone surrogate makes JsonDocument.Parse throw ArgumentException. Both escape `catch (JsonException)`. The first pass did not run adversarial strings against the totality claim.

learned.lesson: An ordinary user's Get-MpPreference hides Defender's list properties behind the string 'N/A: Must be an administrator to view exclusions'. 11 properties carry it, including ControlledFolderAccessAllowedApplications and the DefaultProtectedFolders list, which has different wording. Any count or check of those lists from a non-elevated read counts the notice. Only the 'N/A:' prefix is safe to key on. DefenderState.Count and DefenderStateCorpus.json (P01-P09 placeholder rows, R01-R08 real rows) already do this. Reuse them rather than re-deriving.
learned.evidence: Build measurement (unelevated census, 11 properties carry the placeholder); line reads 'allowed apps=hidden from non-administrators'. Corpus run: plain counting reds P01-P09 and greens R01-R08.

learned.lesson: When a survey quotes a count taken from a reduced-privilege read, ask what the entries were before the count enters a contract. '1 allowed app' was the permission notice, and it went into the Describe contract as the expected reading before anyone looked at the string.
learned.evidence: build-check said 'allowed-apps list has 1 entry' (elevated=False); the design contract expected 'allowed apps=1'; critique M1 and the build's unelevated read showed ['N/A: Must be an administrator to view exclusions'].

learned.lesson: Re-routing an administrator-gated must-verify precondition to the person by documenting it in build does not close its obligation rows. validate-slice halts until the loop waives them. Put such invariants in filed_for_later (who=person) at design time. 'Needs admin, a running Defender or a desktop' is the test for person-only.
learned.evidence: O-014, O-015 and O-016 were routed in code review (m3) and in the build doc; validate-slice #1 halted on them anyway; validate #2 passed only after the waivers to SC-287..SC-289.

learned.lesson: In this project, default-suite Facts that compare a record line to a fresh independent machine read are where red-on-a-valid-machine defects come from. Assert only the one value the Fact is about (the integer equals the fresh read), and cover the shape variance (multi-word AMRunningMode, null fields, foreign module-path entries) as fixed-input Describe rows. The design said 'nothing turns red', yet the two Facts the builder added on top of it were the source of m1 and R2-m4.
learned.evidence: DefenderStateRecordTests.cs:60 (AMRunningMode=\S+ rejects 'Passive Mode', 'SxS Passive Mode', 'EDR Block Mode'); R2-m4 regex measured matching a SQL Server '...\PowerShell\Modules\' entry; both waived to SC-282 and SC-283.

learned.lesson: The repo's idiom for a test that spawns a process is VolumeUsageTests.GetVolumeUsed (async stdout and stderr reads, WaitForExit with a timeout, Kill(entireProcessTree: true)). Do not copy Fsutil in HeldOpenTreeTests.cs, which does ReadToEnd and then WaitForExit() with no timeout. VolumeUsageTests also shows that powershell.exe 5.1 runs fine under testhost's inherited pwsh-7 PSModulePath, so the PSModulePath strip is harmless but not load-bearing.
learned.evidence: VolumeUsageTests.cs:303-321 versus HeldOpenTreeTests.cs:347-349 (review M6); the design had named Fsutil as the idiom.

learned.lesson: Existing temp-route Fitness rules apply to any new file in tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests, even when it only needs a path that does not exist. Path.GetTempPath() broke them in the first build of the missing-exe Fact. Use a name under AppContext.BaseDirectory, or %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp, which is also what lesson #360 prescribes for trees.
learned.evidence: Build stage fixed the one architecture-rule break the engine reported; AnExecutableThatCannotBeStartedIsNotRead passes again after the edit; the rule's patterns match 0 times in the three changed test files.

learned.lesson: Do not design the product's reaction to CFA (skip the keep-last-access open in protected folders, a KnownWorkarounds entry, or reopening Q-159) before the person's results table exists. Spike #109 proves only the open-refused branch (Kept 5 to 4, 55 of 55 entries, 0 unreadable). The open-OK, set-refused branch of TryOpenKeepingLastAccess (SynchronousIoCancel.cs:529-543) has never been exercised and needs a seam that does not exist. The last-access witness in the recipe will show 'moved' for either branch without telling them apart.
learned.evidence: Spike #109 detail ('Not exercised: the branch where the write-attributes open succeeds but SetFileInformationByHandle fails'); validate 'not reached' list; Q-101 still open.

learned.lesson: Size a slice whose changed surface is tests/, docs/ and fitness.yaml, and whose real criteria are person-checked, as 'record plus recipe'. The review load scales with the number of default-suite Facts added, not with product risk. SL-101 added about 65 tests (DefenderStateRecordTests plus a 17-row corpus) and drew 13 findings across 2 critique and 2 code-review rounds, 10 of them minors waived to SC-275..SC-284.
learned.evidence: index shows critique ran 2x, code-review 2x and validate-slice 2x; obligations O-017..O-029 (13 findings); O-020..O-029 map to SC-275, SC-276, SC-277, SC-278, SC-279, SC-282, SC-280, SC-281, SC-283 and SC-284.

unknowns: Does Tamper Protection (on, on this PC) refuse Set-MpPreference -EnableControlledFolderAccess even from an elevated shell? Validate read IsTamperProtected and found no CFA policy key, but never tried the cmdlet. The recipe's Windows Security UI fallback exists, and AuditMode has no UI switch (recalled).

Does ControlledFolderAccessProtectedFolders become the 'N/A:' placeholder for a non-administrator once the list is non-empty? It reads as an empty list here. DefenderState.Describe handles both shapes, but only the recipe's elevated step 1 listing will show which one occurs.

What does the 'Controlled Folder Access:' line look like in HeldOpenTreeTests.Record() on a Windows without Defender? In the Sandbox the HeldOpenTree fixture refuses SYSTEM's temp folder (TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot), so only DefenderStateRecordTests' reads of the same Lazy line were seen there. The line itself was seen there as 'not read (...0x800106ba)'.

Does the default suite stay green on a PC where Defender runs in Passive, SxS Passive or EDR Block mode, or on an older platform where EnableControlledFolderAccess may be null? This is unmeasured. It is the failure mode behind SC-282 and SC-283.

candidates.title: Run the SL-101 CFA recipe as administrator and fill its results table (apply the SC-275 and SC-279 recipe edits first)
candidates.why: SL-101 built only criterion 1. Criteria 2 and 3 (derived, checked_by person) are the answer to Q-101: is the FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES keep-open on a protected folder blocked, does it fall back, does it raise a 1123/1124 event or a toast? They are unanswered at HEAD d79ce14. This PC reads EnableControlledFolderAccess=0 (Disabled), protected folders=0, allowed apps=hidden from non-administrators, AMRunningMode=Normal, platform 4.18.26080.4 (HeldOpenTree output line and an independent powershell.exe 5.1 read). Defender Operational holds 0 events with ID 1123 or 1124 (survey count, non-elevated). The Sandbox cannot host the run: WinDefend and WdFilter START_TYPE 4, start fails with 1058, Get-MpPreference fails with 0x800106ba. The steps are in docs/design/SL-101-controlled-folder-access.md (W-admin arms and disarms, W-user scans). The CFA-off blocks have run once at Medium integrity (every Witness unchanged, Control moved, 15 files, 1 folder, 6280 bytes, 0 unreadable). No CFA-on step has ever run. The same session discharges the waived preconditions SC-287 (unsigned published exe is the image CFA judges), SC-288 (custom versus default protected folder) and SC-289 (the person can arm CFA). Land the recipe edits SC-275 (use C:\Users\Public\Documents\fsa-cfa-<hex>\R as the primary fixture, which is in CFA's default protected set) and SC-279 (list allowed apps by name before and after, void on an existing match) first, because they change steps 1-2 and the session spends the one administrator window. Its result decides whether a follow-up product slice exists at all (skip the keep-open in protected folders, a KnownWorkarounds entry, or reopening Q-159).
